note: Source manifest for the ORCH-753 gold cohort. The paper text is NOT committed; it lives at C:/t/eval-fulltext/<PMCID>.txt and gold.load_fulltext refuses a text whose sha256 differs.
citation: Wissbroecker KB et al. Biochemical and genomic evidence for converging metabolic routes of metformin and biguanide breakdown in environmental Pseudomonads The Journal of biological chemistry 2024.
pathway_in_one_line: Two convergent bacterial routes that funnel the drug metformin and the parent compound biguanide into guanylurea and then guanidine for nitrogen assimilation.
scope_note: In scope: metformin -> guanylurea + dimethylamine (heteromeric metforminase MfmAB), biguanide -> guanylurea (novel aminohydrolase BguH), guanylurea -> guanidine (GuuH), and BguH acting on N-methylbiguanide at ~1% the biguanide rate. In scope as a PROPOSED but not demonstrated route: metformin -> N-methylbiguanide -> biguanide by successive N-demethylation; the paper is explicit that the demethylase was not found, so this must not be booked as a measured step. Adjacent: the ureohydrolase family context (arginase, agmatinase, five-oxoprolinase PxpBC), the downstream guanidine assimilation pathway, and the metal-dependence enzymology.
selected_because: A bacterial metabolic paper deliberately unlike the existing enterobactin and menaquinone golds: a short degradative pathway with a small cast of small molecules, so a gold reviewer can hand-check it in one sitting. It also supplies two things the current gold lacks entirely - a conversion the paper proposes but refuses to claim, and a measured side-activity - which is exactly where the review_required / off-pathway machinery should be exercised.
